  Node 22.13 to 24).
- **Key:** an API key of that provider or gateway (`doz account add NAME --provider xai` — or `openrouter`, `vercel-ai-gateway`, `google`; `--api-key` for Anthropic, `--openai-key` for OpenAI); the sandbox only gets a placeholder.
- **Set up for you:** its telemetry off (`telemetrySetting: disabled` — Dirac sends events to dirac.run by default)
  and its self-update off (`DIRAC_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`).
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given (any of those it can use, so you can switch).
- **Use:** `dirac` (a session; with approvals off, `--auto-approve-all`), or `dirac --yolo "…"` for one task.

## Kimi Code (Moonshot AI)

Moonshot AI's terminal agent, the successor to kimi-cli (`doz try kimi-code`, or `kimi`). Kimi Code takes its model
from the environment (`KIMI_MODEL_*`), and Dozable names the provider or gateway you choose: **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **xAI** (the default), **Google AI**, **OpenRouter** or **Vercel AI Gateway** (`--provider` / `--gateway`, or the Quick try's “Where it gets its model”; `--model` picks the model). On xAI the
model is `grok-build-0.1`. Kimi's own models need a Kimi account or a Moonshot key, which Dozable does not hold yet.

- **Installed** from the npm registry, integrity-checked. Node 22 on the Node and Debian bases (not Alpine: it needs
  Node 22.19 or later).
- **Key:** an API key of that provider or gateway (a placeholder in the sandbox, in its own variable and in
  `KIMI_MODEL_API_KEY`), read on each request and never written into `~/.kimi-code/config.toml`.
- **Set up for you:** its telemetry and self-update off (`KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`). At each
  start it asks Moonshot for its public client settings; Dozable keeps that request out quietly, and Kimi Code does
  without them. Its first start in a folder asks whether to trust it.
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given (any of those it can use, so you can switch).
- **Use:** `kimi` (a session; with approvals off, `--auto`), or `kimi -p "…"` for one task.

## Cline CLI (Cline)

Cline's terminal agent (`doz try cline`), on the key of the provider or gateway you choose: **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **xAI** (the default), **Google AI**, **OpenRouter** or **Vercel AI Gateway** — no Cline account.
Dozable puts the provider and model on its command line (`cline -P xai -m grok-build-0.1` on xAI).

- **Installed** from the npm registry's linux-arm64 package, integrity-checked. Debian and Node bases (not Alpine).
- **Key:** an API key of that provider or gateway (`doz account add NAME --provider xai` — or `openrouter`, `vercel-ai-gateway`, `google`; `--api-key` for Anthropic, `--openai-key` for OpenAI); the sandbox only gets a placeholder.
- **Set up for you:** its telemetry and self-update off (`telemetryOptOut`, `autoUpdateEnabled: false`,
  `CLINE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`), and its ClinePass notice. When it starts it asks for feature flags (its PostHog host), its
  recommended models (api.cline.bot) and the models.dev catalogue; Dozable keeps those requests out quietly, and Cline
  does without them. Cline approves its own tool calls by default (its
  `--auto-approve` is on unless you pass `--auto-approve false`).
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given (any of those it can use, so you can switch).
- **Use:** `cline` (a session), or `cline "…"` for one task.

## OpenHands CLI (OpenHands)

OpenHands' terminal agent (`doz try openhands`). Its LLM settings come from the environment (`--override-with-envs`,
in Dozable's command), set for the provider or gateway you choose: **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **xAI** (the default), **Google AI**, **OpenRouter** or **Vercel AI Gateway** (`--provider` / `--gateway`, or the Quick try's “Where it gets its model”; `--model` picks the model). On xAI the model is `grok-build-0.1`.
Nothing is written to its settings.

- **Installed** from its GitHub release (the linux-arm64 build), checked against the SHA-512 Dozable recorded. Debian and
  Node bases (not Alpine: OpenHands publishes a glibc build only).
- **Key:** an API key of that provider or gateway (`LLM_API_KEY` and its own variable, the same placeholder in the
  sandbox). OpenHands Cloud's sign-in is not offered.
- **Set up for you:** its model price list read locally (`LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP`, not fetched from GitHub) and
  its banner off.
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given (any of those it can use), and two reads no setting
  turns off: its public skills (a git clone of
  github.com/OpenHands/extensions at each start) and its latest release on PyPI (a notice only; Dozable installs the
  pinned release).
- **Use:** `openhands` (a session; with approvals off, `--always-approve`), or
  `openhands --override-with-envs --headless -t "…"` for one task.

Letta's memory-first coding agent (`doz try letta-code`, or `letta`) on its **local backend** — no Letta account, its
agents and memory kept in the sandbox (`~/.letta`) — on the key of the provider or gateway you choose: **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **xAI** (the default), **Google AI**, **OpenRouter** or **Vercel AI Gateway** (on xAI the model is `xai/grok-4.3`; `grok-build-0.1` is
not in its catalogue).

  Node 22.19 or later).

- **Set up for you:** its telemetry and self-update off (`LETTA_CODE_TELEM=0`, `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`). When its TUI
  starts it may ask Letta Cloud for its health and an account balance; Dozable keeps those requests out quietly, and it
  does without them. Letta asks before running commands (its own default).
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given (any of those it can use, so you can switch).

  catalogue; Dozable keeps that request out quietly, and it does without it.
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given (any of those it can use, so you can switch).
- **Use:** `docker-agent` (a session; with approvals off, `--yolo`), or
  `docker-agent run coder --exec "…"` for one task.

- **Installed** from PyPI into its own Python environment: Dozable's Python and exactly the packages Dozable locked, each
  checked against its recorded hash. Debian and Node bases (not Alpine yet).
- **Key:** an API key of that provider or gateway (`doz account add NAME --provider xai` — or `openrouter`, `vercel-ai-gateway`, `google`; `--api-key` for Anthropic, `--openai-key` for OpenAI); the sandbox only gets a placeholder.
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given (any of those it can use, so you can switch). Its update check and its model catalogue refresh are turned off.
- **Use:** `tau` (a session), or `tau -p "…"` for one task.

## Gemini CLI (Google) — superseded

Superseded by Antigravity CLI: Google retired Gemini CLI for personal accounts; it still works with a **paid** Gemini
API key. Dozable keeps it, listed after the current agents; `doz try gemini` says so first.

- **Installed** from the npm registry, integrity-checked. Node, Debian and Alpine (on Alpine its shell tool runs
  without a terminal).
- **Key:** a Gemini API key, as Antigravity CLI. Never the Google sign-in (Google's terms forbid third-party tools from
  using it).
- **Set up for you:** approval prompts off, usage statistics off, auto-update off.

## Coming: CodeBuddy Code, Every Code

Two agents Dozable had recipes for are **coming** again, because their first screen is a sign-in Dozable cannot offer
(`doz search` says why):

- **CodeBuddy Code** (Tencent) asks you to sign in to a CodeBuddy account at its first screen, even with Dozable's model
  set.
- **Every Code** (just-every, a Codex CLI fork) shows a ChatGPT sign-in whenever it has no login file, whatever
  provider is set.

Each comes back when it can start on the model Dozable gives it.

## What each one calls — the network profiles

Dozable keeps a **network profile** of every agent: a fresh try with the network open and every request logged, its
first start and a short task, and for each host and path it called, a decision — allowed (and why), allowed by its
path only, turned off by the agent's own setting, or refused. The recipes are checked against these profiles on every
build, so an agent never meets a refusal on a normal first run, and a new release is profiled again before anything
new is allowed (`make profile-agents` in the source tree; `make agent-currency` says which agents moved).

## Is it current?

`doz search`, `doz try` and the Quick try show each agent's **latest release** as your Mac last saw it — the version,
the day it came out, how long ago, and **active** (a release in the last 3 months), **quiet** (none for 3),
**stale** (none for 6) or **deprecated** by its maker — and its **standing**: current, or superseded by another
agent. See [Is it current?](https://dozable.com/docs/try-and-search.md#is-it-supported-doz-search).

---

URL: https://dozable.com/docs/ai-tools

# Other AI tools

Beside the coding agents, Dozable runs AI tools that are not coding agents: command-line tools that answer a prompt,
prompt toolkits, agent frameworks. Each is tried like an agent (`doz try TOOL`) and uses an **API key** of a provider
or a **gateway** Dozable offers. The key stays on your Mac; the sandbox only gets a placeholder, which Dozable's proxy swaps
for the key on the way out, and only to that provider's or gateway's own API.

```sh
doz try fabric                                  # Fabric, on its default (a Google AI key)
doz try shell-gpt --provider openai             # ShellGPT on an OpenAI key
doz try gptme --gateway openrouter --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6
doz try aichat --dry-run                        # the plan: its model, and every provider and gateway it can use
doz try stitch                                  # Google Stitch's command line, on a Stitch API key
doz search gemini                               # what Dozable runs with a Google key
```

## Providers and gateways

Most tools here can talk to more than one: **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **xAI**, **Google AI** (the Gemini API), and the
gateways **OpenRouter** and **Vercel AI Gateway** (one key, many models — their model names are `creator/name`). Which
ones depends on the tool: each section below lists them, its default first. Choose one with `--provider` (or
`--gateway`) on `doz try`, `doz new`, `doz create` and `doz up`, or in the Quick try's setup (“Where TOOL gets its model”, then the model picker) and New Sandbox, or in doz_project.yaml (`model_source:`, `model:`);
`--model` picks the model (the default is the provider's or gateway's: `grok-4-1-fast`, `gpt-5.4-mini`,
`gemini-2.5-flash`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` …).

- **The key is a key of that provider or gateway**: `doz account add NAME --provider openrouter` (or
  `vercel-ai-gateway`, `xai`, `google`), `--api-key` for Anthropic, `--openai-key` for OpenAI — never a Claude
  subscription or a ChatGPT sign-in. The sandbox's account decides which one it talks to; `doz account use NAME ACCOUNT`
  switches it (from its next session).
- **Dozable sets the tool's own settings** for the choice (a base URL, a model, its provider switch) at every session and
  `doz exec` — a value you set yourself wins — and nothing is baked into the image, so one image serves every choice.
- **The key only ever goes to that provider's or gateway's own hosts.** The tool may reach the others' (so you can
  switch), but a placeholder sent to any other host is refused.
- The default models were chosen from the providers' published names; a model a provider has renamed or retired is
  refused by the provider itself — choose another with `--model`.

### Which models: `doz models`

```sh
doz models --gateway openrouter               # OpenRouter's models: id, context, price in and out per million tokens, tools
doz models --gateway vercel-ai-gateway sonnet # Vercel AI Gateway's, narrowed to those matching "sonnet"
doz models --gateway openrouter --refresh     # read the list again now
doz models --provider xai                     # a provider: the model Dozable checked
```

- **A gateway publishes its list**, and Dozable reads it on this Mac — never from a sandbox — at most once a day, keeping
  the last one (offline, the last list stays; `--refresh` reads it now and starts Dozable's background process when it
  is not running). `--json` gives it as data.
- **A provider lists its models only with a key**, so `doz models` shows the model Dozable checked for it; any other id
  that provider names may still be given with `--model`.
- **A `--model` a gateway does not list is used as given**, with a note on the closest ids it does list:
  `note: openai/gpt-5.4-mni is not in OpenRouter's model list — did you mean openai/gpt-5.4-mini, …? (used as given)`.
  Lists change every week, so it is never refused for that.

A tool that answers and exits opens a **shell** as its session, with the tool on the PATH. Type its commands there.

## OpenClaw

A self-hosted personal agent with shell and file tools. Its own docs recommend running it isolated: in a sandbox its
tools act on the sandbox, not your Mac.

- **Installed** from the npm registry, integrity-checked, on Node 24, which Dozable installs for it (Debian-based bases
  only). The image is large (about 1.3 GB).
- **Key:** Google AI (default), Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI or OpenRouter — OpenClaw's own providers, which read the key's
  usual variable. Its models are `provider/model` (`google/gemini-2.5-flash` by default); Dozable puts the chosen one in
  `DOZ_MODEL`.
- **Use:** one headless turn — `openclaw agent exec "a task" --auth-env-only --model "$DOZ_MODEL"`. Its auto-update is
  off (`OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`).
- **May reach:** those providers' APIs (the key goes to the chosen one only).
- **Later:** its Gateway (the TUI, the Control UI on port 18789, chat channels such as Telegram or Slack) is a
  background service with a web page, which Dozable does not run or forward yet. You can start it by hand in a second
  session (`openclaw gateway`), but nothing keeps it running and the Control UI is not reachable from the Mac.

## nanobot

A small personal agent in the terminal (an OpenClaw-style assistant its authors keep auditable).

- **Installed** from PyPI with every dependency pinned by its hash, on Dozable's own Python (Debian-based bases).
- **Key:** xAI (default), OpenAI, Google AI, OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway. nanobot is set up with its custom
  OpenAI-compatible provider whose base URL, key and model come from `DOZ_MODEL_BASE_URL`, `DOZ_MODEL_API_KEY` and
  `DOZ_MODEL`, which Dozable sets for the choice (`~/.nanobot/config.json`, keys written only when not there yet).
- **Use:** `nanobot` opens its terminal UI (the session); one headless turn is `nanobot agent -m "a task"`.
- **May reach:** those providers' and gateways' APIs, and OpenAI's public tokenizer file (`openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/encodings/…`), which
  the token counter it uses downloads at the first turn.
- **Later:** its gateway (chat channels) and web UI need a background service and a forwarded port.

## gptme

A terminal agent with shell, Python and file tools.

- **Installed** from PyPI with every dependency pinned by its hash, on Dozable's own Python (Debian-based bases).
- **Key:** xAI (default), Anthropic, OpenAI, Google AI, OpenRouter, or Vercel AI Gateway (through its OpenAI-compatible
  `local` provider). Dozable sets `MODEL` to `provider/model` for the choice (or `--model`).
- **Set up for you:** its confirmation prompts off (`--no-confirm`; `gptme.permissions = ask` keeps them).
- **Use:** `gptme` (the session); one headless run is `gptme --non-interactive "a task"`.
- **May reach:** those providers' and gateways' APIs, and OpenAI's public tokenizer file (as nanobot).
- **Later:** its browser tool needs Chromium in the image; `gptme-server`'s web UI needs a forwarded port.

## llm

Simon Willison's command-line tool for prompting models (and logging every prompt to SQLite).

- **Installed** from PyPI with every dependency pinned by its hash, on Dozable's own Python (Debian-based bases), with the
  `llm-grok` plugin, which talks to xAI.
- **Key:** xAI (default, through `llm-grok`) or OpenAI (its own models). Dozable sets `LLM_MODEL` to the chosen model.
- **Use:** the session is a shell. `llm "a question"` (or `-m MODEL`).
- **May reach:** xAI's and OpenAI's APIs. Other providers need plugins, which are not in the image.
- **Later:** `llm install` (more plugins) needs PyPI at run time, which no permission offers yet.

## ShellGPT

A command-line assistant (`sgpt`) that answers questions and turns requests into shell commands (`sgpt --shell`).

- **Installed** from PyPI with every dependency pinned by its hash, on Dozable's own Python (Debian-based bases).
- **Key:** xAI (default), OpenAI, Google AI (its OpenAI-compatible endpoint), OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway. ShellGPT
  speaks OpenAI's API; Dozable points it at the choice (`API_BASE_URL`, `DEFAULT_MODEL`) and puts the key's placeholder
  under `OPENAI_API_KEY` too — it still works only on the chosen API.
- **Use:** the session is a shell. `sgpt "a question"`, `sgpt --shell "find large files"`.
- **May reach:** those providers' and gateways' APIs.

## ZeroClaw

A personal-agent runtime in one Rust program, with shell, file and web tools.

- **Installed** from the project's linux-arm64 release on GitHub, checked against the SHA-512 Dozable recorded (Debian-based
  bases).
- **Key:** xAI (default), OpenAI, Google AI, OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway. ZeroClaw is set up
  (`~/.zeroclaw/config.toml`, keys written only when not there yet) with one OpenAI-shaped provider and one agent,
  `main`, at full autonomy — the sandbox is the boundary. Dozable points the provider at the choice (its uri, model and the
  key's placeholder) through ZeroClaw's own environment overrides.
- **Use:** the session is `zeroclaw agent -a main`; one headless turn is `zeroclaw agent -a main -m "a task"`.
- **May reach:** those providers' and gateways' APIs.
- **Later:** its gateway, web dashboard and chat channels need a background service and a forwarded port.

## AIChat

An all-in-one LLM command line: a chat REPL, a shell assistant (`-e`), roles, sessions.

- **Installed** from the project's static linux-arm64 release on GitHub, checked against the SHA-512 Dozable recorded.
  Every base, Alpine included.
- **Key:** xAI (default), Anthropic, OpenAI, Google AI or OpenRouter — its built-in clients, with no config file
  (`AICHAT_PROVIDER`, `AICHAT_MODEL`: `xai:grok-4-1-fast` by default, or `-m`).
- **Use:** the session is its REPL; one question is `aichat "a question"`, a shell command `aichat -e "list big files"`.
- **May reach:** those providers' APIs.
- **Its playground:** run `aichat --serve` in a session; the sandbox's **Open AIChat web** button (or
  `doz open NAME`) opens it in your Mac's browser — see [Web ports](https://dozable.com/docs/web-ports.md).

## tgpt

A small terminal chat client.

- **Installed** from the project's static linux-arm64 release on GitHub, checked against the SHA-512 Dozable recorded.
  Every base, Alpine included.
- **Providers:** **Google AI** (the default — its Gemini provider, `AI_PROVIDER=gemini`), **OpenAI**, **xAI**,
  **OpenRouter** and **Vercel AI Gateway** (its OpenAI provider at the chosen source's chat endpoint, `OPENAI_URL`,
  `OPENAI_MODEL`).
- **Key:** an API key of that provider or gateway (a placeholder in the sandbox). On Google AI, Dozable's proxy sends the
  key as Google's `x-goog-api-key` header — checked against a stand-in provider, not yet against Google itself.
- **Use:** the session is its interactive mode (`tgpt -i`); one question is `tgpt -q "a question"`.
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given. Its key-less "free" providers are other companies' services, which Dozable does not allow
  by default.

## smolagents

Hugging Face's library for agents that write and run Python, with its `smolagent` command. Its own README says its
built-in Python executor is not a security boundary and recommends a sandbox — this is one.

- **Installed** from PyPI (with its toolkit and OpenAI extras) with every dependency pinned by its hash, on Dozable's own
  Python (Debian-based bases).
- **Key:** xAI (default), OpenAI, Google AI, OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway, through its OpenAI-compatible model:
  `smolagent "a task" --model-type OpenAIModel --model-id "$DOZ_MODEL" --api-base "$OPENAI_BASE_URL"` (Dozable sets both
  for the choice; the key's placeholder is also `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
- **Set up for you:** Hugging Face Hub telemetry off (`HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY`).
- **Use:** the session is a shell.
- **May reach:** those providers' and gateways' APIs. Its web-search tools reach the open web only when you allow it.

## Agent Development Kit (Google)

Google's Python framework for building agents (`adk`).

- **Installed** from PyPI with every dependency pinned by its hash, on Dozable's own Python (Debian-based bases).
- **Key:** a Gemini API key, read by Google's genai SDK (`GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=FALSE`: the API key, never Vertex AI).
- **Use:** the session is a shell. Write an agent (a Python package folder whose agent module defines `root_agent`), then
  `adk run FOLDER` talks to it in the terminal.
- **May reach:** the Gemini API.
- **Later:** `adk web` (its dev UI) and `adk api_server` need a forwarded port.

## promptfoo

A command line for evaluating and red-teaming prompts and LLM apps. A red-team run sends attack prompts with your key —
in a sandbox the key stays on the Mac.

- **Installed** from the npm registry, integrity-checked, on Node 22 (Debian-based bases).
- **Key:** xAI (default), OpenAI, Google AI, OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway: its `openai` provider is pointed at the
  choice (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, the key under `OPENAI_API_KEY`) — `providers: ["openai:chat:MODEL"]` in a config, the model
  in `DOZ_MODEL`; on xAI its `xai` provider works too.
- **Set up for you:** its telemetry and update check off (`PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_UPDATE`).
- **Use:** the session is a shell. `promptfoo eval -c promptfooconfig.yaml`.
- **May reach:** those providers' and gateways' APIs. **Kept out, quietly:** `r.promptfoo.app` — with its telemetry off, promptfoo still sends one
  "telemetry disabled" event each run; no setting stops it, so Dozable refuses it without counting it as a refusal.
- **Later:** `promptfoo view` (its web viewer) needs a forwarded port.

## clai (Pydantic AI)

Pydantic AI's command line for chatting with models.

- **Installed** from PyPI with every dependency pinned by its hash, on Dozable's own Python (Debian-based bases).
- **Providers:** **xAI** (the default), **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **Google AI**, **OpenRouter** and **Vercel AI
  Gateway** — Pydantic AI's OpenAI-compatible model at the chosen source's base URL (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`), or its
  Anthropic model (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`). Dozable puts the model on its command line (`-m openai-chat:MODEL`; on xAI,
  `grok-4-1-fast`), unless you give your own `-m`.
- **Key:** an API key of that provider or gateway (a placeholder in the sandbox, also under `OPENAI_API_KEY` or
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).
- **Use:** one question is `clai --no-stream "a question"`.
- **May reach:** the API of the provider or gateway it was given.
- **Later:** `clai web` (its chat page) needs a forwarded port.

## Fabric

A prompt toolkit: crowd-sourced "patterns" applied to text you pipe in.

- **Installed** from the project's own linux-arm64 release on GitHub, checked against the SHA-512 Dozable recorded when it
  pinned the release. Debian, Node and Alpine bases.
- **Key:** Google AI (default: `doz account add google --provider google`; get one at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey),
  Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI or OpenRouter — its own vendors. Dozable sets `DEFAULT_VENDOR` and `DEFAULT_MODEL` for the choice
  (over the ones in `~/.config/fabric/.env`, written only when not there yet).
- **Patterns** come with it: its release's some 260 patterns, checksum-verified when the image is prepared, in
  `/opt/fabric/patterns` (`CUSTOM_PATTERNS_DIRECTORY`) — `fabric -l` lists them; `fabric -U` (from GitHub) is not needed.
- **Use:** `echo "some text" | fabric "summarise this"`, `cat notes.txt | fabric -p summarize` — or the sandbox page's Guide.
- **May reach:** those providers' APIs.
- **Its REST API:** run `fabric --serve` in a session; the sandbox's **Open Fabric REST API** button (or `doz open NAME`)
  opens its API reference in your Mac's browser — see [Web ports](https://dozable.com/docs/web-ports.md).

## Google Stitch CLI

Google Labs' command line for Stitch, Google's UI design service: it generates and edits app screens from a prompt (on
Google's side, with Gemini) and prints their ids and links. It is a client of the hosted service — every command is a
call to Stitch.

- **Installed** from the npm registry, integrity-checked, on Node 22 (Debian-based bases).
- **Key:** a **Stitch API key** (it starts `AQ.`), made in Stitch's settings at https://stitch.withgoogle.com —
  `doz account add stitch --provider google-stitch --no-verify`. Not a Gemini or Google Cloud key (`AIza…`), which Stitch
  refuses. Generation uses your Stitch account's quota.
- **Not offered:** its Google sign-in (`stitch login`), which would keep Google tokens in the sandbox. The API key covers
  projects, screens and design systems.
- **Use:** the session is a shell. `stitch find projects --json`;
  `stitch generate screen --new-project "My app" --prompt "A sign-up screen" --device MOBILE`. Every command takes
  `--json` and `--dry-run`.
- **May reach:** Stitch's API only (`stitch.googleapis.com`). It has no update check; its client header's telemetry is off.
- **Preview:** `stitch serve -p PROJECT --port 3000` serves a project's screens; `doz ports add NAME 3000` opens them on
  your Mac — see [Web ports](https://dozable.com/docs/web-ports.md).

URL: https://dozable.com/docs/web-ports

# Web ports: opening a sandbox's web page on your Mac

Some tools serve a web page from inside the sandbox: a chat playground, a workflow editor, the dev server of the app
you are building. A **forward** makes such a port reachable in your Mac's browser, at `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/` —
on this Mac only, never on your network.

```sh
doz ports my-app                 # the sandbox's forwarded ports: each one's URL on this Mac and whether it listens
doz ports add my-app 3000        # forward the dev server on port 3000 too (kept until you remove it)
doz open my-app                  # open its first web port in your browser
doz open my-app 3000 --print     # or print the URL
doz ports rm my-app 3000         # stop forwarding it
```

In the dashboard, a sandbox's header has an **Open** button for each web port while the sandbox runs, and its
Overview tab lists every forward with its state.

## Where the ports come from

- **The tool's own.** A tool whose recipe declares a web port gets it forwarded in every sandbox made from it — for
  example AIChat's playground (`aichat --serve`, port 8000, opened at `/playground`). Run the server in a session;
  its Open button works as soon as it listens.
- **Yours.** `doz ports add NAME PORT` forwards any port a program you start listens on — a dev server, a notebook,
  a dashboard. `--title` names its button; `--path` is what `doz open` opens. At most 16 per sandbox.

## When it listens

A forward listens **while the sandbox runs**. When the sandbox stops, sleeps or hibernates, its listeners close at
once; when it starts or wakes again — and after Dozable itself restarts — they come back by themselves. `doz ports`
says `stopped` until then.

The port on your Mac is the sandbox's own when it is free. When another program on your Mac already uses it (or it is
below 1024), Dozable picks a free one, says so (`moved`), and keeps it for next time.

## What a forward can and cannot do

- **This Mac only.** It listens on `127.0.0.1` (and `::1`), never on the network. Other programs on this Mac can reach
  it, as they can any local server — a tool with its own sign-in still asks for it.
- **Inbound only.** It carries your browser's requests to the program in the sandbox. It does not let the sandbox
  reach anything: what the program itself may reach is still decided by the sandbox's [network](https://dozable.com/docs/permissions-and-network.md).
- **No key crosses it.** Your keys are swapped in by Dozable's proxy only on the sandbox's own outbound requests; a
  forward never touches them. A page that shows its environment shows a placeholder, which is useless anywhere else.
- **From another device** (the dashboard through [`doz serve`](https://dozable.com/docs/doz-serve.md)), `127.0.0.1` is that device, not your
  Mac: the button says the port is on the Mac instead of opening it there.

How it works: each connection your browser makes is relayed into the sandbox by Dozable's small helper there, to the
program's own `localhost`. A program that listens on `127.0.0.1` or `0.0.0.0` inside the sandbox both work.

---

URL: https://dozable.com/privacy

# Dozable Privacy Policy

**Last updated:** 16 October 2026

Dozable is made by **Roundrect Pty Ltd** (ABN 36 613 522 277), Queensland, Australia ("we", "us"). This policy explains what Dozable and dozable.com collect, why, and how to turn it off.

## In short

- **Your work stays on your Mac.** Dozable never collects anything from inside your sandboxes — not your code, files, prompts, commands' arguments, terminal output, sandbox names, paths, the sites your sandboxes reach, or your accounts and keys. Your API keys never leave your Mac.
- **Official builds send anonymous usage statistics** — counts and ranges about how Dozable itself is used, at most once a day — so we can see what to fix and improve. It is **on by default and easy to turn off** (below). You can see exactly what would be sent with `doz telemetry show`.
- **Signing up is optional.** If you give us your email, we use it only for what you ticked, and you can unsubscribe from any email in one click.
- **Builds from the open-source repository send nothing.** The statistics and sign-up code is part of the official builds only and is not open source.

## What gets collected

### 1. Anonymous usage statistics (official builds)

**When:** at most one message per day on days you use Dozable, plus one when you first run a new version. Sent in the background; if your Mac is offline, it is retried and dropped after 7 days.

**Identifier:** a random install ID created on your Mac (not linked to you, your email, your Mac's serial number or name). Reset it any time with `doz telemetry reset`.

**What is sent — the complete list:**

| About | Exactly what |
|---|---|
| The version | Dozable's version, release channel (stable, beta, canary), how it was installed (Homebrew or download), and the version you upgraded from |
| Your Mac | macOS major version (e.g. 26), chip family (e.g. M3), memory as a range (e.g. 16 GB, 24 GB, 64 GB+), CPU cores as a range |
| Commands | how many times each Dozable command was used that day (e.g. `create`: 2, `hibernate`: 3) — the command's name only, never its arguments |
| Failures | how many times a command failed and its exit code (a number), never the error text |
| Getting started | whether setup was done in the terminal or the dashboard, how far it got, and roughly how long until the first sandbox session (e.g. under 5 minutes) |
| Sandboxes created | how many were created with each agent (Claude Code, Codex, pi, none), each base image from Dozable's own list (custom Dockerfiles are counted only as "dockerfile"), each account type (this Mac's login, API key, setup token, none) and each network preset (standard, locked, open, custom) |
| Size of your setup, as ranges | how many sandboxes you keep, how many ran at once, how many restore points, total disk used (e.g. 5–20 GB) |
| Speed | typical and slow times for starting, waking, hibernating and pausing a sandbox that day, rounded to 50 ms |
| Reliability | how many wakes failed, sandboxes restored after a crash, host crashes, and which built-in image-preparation step failed |
| Features used | whether the dashboard, the installed dashboard app and `doz serve` were used, how many other devices are connected (as a range), whether workspace rules are in use, the GitHub access mode (off, read, push), whether an agent reported its status, how many restore points and templates were made, and your update setting |
| Time | how long sandboxes ran and slept, as counts of ranges (e.g. three ran for 5–30 minutes), how old sandboxes were when deleted, total running time and how long agents reported working, as ranges, and how many sandboxes were left running over 8 hours with no activity |

**Added by our server:** your **country**, worked out from the connection when the message arrives. ** We do not store your IP address.**

**Never collected:** the names of your sandboxes, images or projects; file or folder names and paths; anything inside a sandbox; anything you type or that a program prints; command arguments; Dockerfile contents; hostnames, websites or network rules; account names, emails or keys; exact times of day you worked; or any hash or fingerprint of your work.

**Why:** to see how Dozable is used and how well it performs in practice — which features to improve, what fails, what is slow, and what defaults to choose. **Lawful basis (EU/UK GDPR):** our legitimate interest in maintaining and improving the software, balanced by the data being minimal, anonymous and easy to turn off.

**Turning it off** — any one of these stops all sending:

- `doz config set telemetry.send_anonymous_usage_stats false` (or the switch in the dashboard's Settings),
- the environment variable `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`,
- `--no-send-anonymous-usage-stats` on a single command.

The first time an official build runs, it prints one line saying statistics are on and how to turn them off.

### 2. Sign-up (optional)

If you sign up — in Dozable's setup, with `doz signup`, or on dozable.com/signup — we keep your **email address**, what you asked for (** release news**, ** tool news**, ** early access**, ** tips and tricks**), and when you signed up, confirmed and (if you do) unsubscribed. We send a confirmation email first; nothing else is sent until you confirm. Every email has a one-click unsubscribe link. We never sell or share your email, and never link it to your usage statistics. The emails are the posts of our [blog](https://dozable.com/blog/index.md), sent only for the topics you ticked. They contain no open or click tracking. To send each one once and to stop sending to addresses that bounce or report spam, we keep a record of which posts were sent to your address and when, and whether one bounced or was reported; this record is deleted with your sign-up.

### 3. The website and the update feed

- **dozable.com** uses no analytics, advertising or tracking scripts, and sets no cookies of its own — the blog included. Our host, Cloudflare, may set a strictly necessary security cookie and keeps standard request logs under [its own privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/). The colour picker on the site exists only when you open it on your own computer.
- **Update checks:** Dozable checks `updates.dozersandbox.com` for new releases at most once a day (or when you ask). That request carries Dozable's version and channel in its user agent and nothing else. It is part of keeping Dozable up to date, not the usage statistics; turn it off with `doz config set updates.mode off`.

## Where it is kept, and for how long

| What | Where | Kept |
|---|---|---|
| Usage statistics | Cloudflare: Workers Analytics Engine (global) and D1 (Oceania region) | raw messages up to 90 days; daily totals that cannot identify an install, indefinitely |
| Sign-up details | Cloudflare D1; emails sent through **Resend** (Resend, Inc., USA; sent from its Tokyo, Japan region) | until you unsubscribe or ask us to delete them; deleted within 30 days of a request (usually at once) |

Our service providers — **Cloudflare** (hosting, statistics storage) and **Resend** (sending email) — process data only on our behalf. Their servers may be outside your country (including the United States and Japan); we rely on their standard contractual protections for these transfers.

## Your choices and rights

You can turn statistics off at any time (above), reset your install ID, unsubscribe from any email, or ask us to access, correct or delete your sign-up details by writing to **privacy@dozersandbox.com**. Because the statistics are anonymous, we cannot find "your" statistics without your install ID — `doz telemetry show` prints it if you want us to delete its records. If you are in the EU or UK, you also have the right to object, to restrict processing and to complain to your data protection authority; in Australia, you can complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC). Signing up is based on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time by unsubscribing.

## Children

Dozable is a developer tool, not intended for children under 16, and we do not knowingly collect their information.

## Changes

If we change what is collected, we will update this page and the list Dozable shows in `doz telemetry show`, and note the change in the release notes. A change that collects more will never apply to data already sent.
